prompts.title: Frame product page
prompts.summary: Writes one frame's product page from its measurements, material and the face shapes it suits.
prompts.prompt:
You write product pages for [brand], a small eyewear brand. Our voice: [three words]. Write the page for the [frame name] frame.

Facts (use only these):
- Material: [acetate, titanium...]
- Colors: [list]
- Lens width / bridge / temple: [mm]
- Face shapes it suits: [list]
- Price: [$]

Give me: a two-line opener that says who the frame is for, a fit section in plain words ("sits a little wide, good for a broad face"), one paragraph on how it is made, and three short answers to the questions people ask before buying frames online. No claims about vision, prescriptions or eye health.
prompts.use: Paste into Claude or ChatGPT once per frame. Keep the fit section; it answers the question that stops most online frame orders.

prompts.title: Fit guide from your measurements
prompts.summary: Turns your frame measurements into a fit guide a buyer can check against glasses they already own.
prompts.prompt:
Here are the measurements for every frame we sell: [paste lens width, bridge, temple, frame width for each]. Write a one-page fit guide for our site.

1. Explain the three numbers printed inside a pair of glasses, in one sentence each.
2. Tell a buyer how to compare them with a pair they own.
3. Sort our frames into narrow, medium and wide, with the numbers that put them there.
4. End with what to do if they sit between two sizes.

Short sentences. No medical or prescription advice.
prompts.use: Put it on its own page and link it from every product page.

prompts.title: Try-on video brief
prompts.summary: A 15-second try-on brief for one frame: the faces, the light, the first second and the shot order.
prompts.prompt:
Write a 15-second try-on video brief for the [frame name] frame from [brand]. We film on a phone.

Include: who wears it on camera (face shape, style), where (window light, time of day), the first second (the frame going on, no logo card), five shots in order with what each one shows, the on-screen words (six words at most), and one line of caption. No music cues that need a license. No claims about vision.
prompts.use: Film three of these per new colorway: one for the product page, two for Reels and TikTok.
